## What you did

- Implemented SAML assertion signature verification with signxml: assertion-level signatures only, SHA-256+ (no legacy SHA-1 flag), per-tenant IdP certificates, rejection of unsigned/wrapped assertions, plus replay protection on assertion IDs via an in-memory cache [2]
- Made the SAML ACS tests deterministic with freezegun instead of sleeps, cleared ruff 0.8 and mypy on `kestrel/auth`, and made a missing Issuer or Subject return a 401 instead of a 500 [1]
- Split the 900-line `saml_utils.py` into `kestrel/auth/saml/{assertions,metadata,bindings}.py` behind a compatibility shim, with the full suite green (1,284 passed) [1]

## What changed

- Maya approved and merged #418; it goes out with tonight's staging deploy, so Fernhill's signature validation is no longer blocked on review [3]

## What is still open

- #423 needs rework: Tom Becker asked to split the module move from the lint fixes into two separate PRs — he'll approve both today [4]
- Fernhill's end-to-end SSO walkthrough is Thursday 10am NY with their Okta tenant; Priya runs the demo and you're on the call, so confirm signature validation is live on staging after tonight's deploy [1][3]
- The replay cache for assertion IDs is still process-local: it needs Redis (`SET NX EX`, keyed by tenant + assertion ID, TTL `NotOnOrAfter` + skew) before multi-pod protection holds — the task you set for today [1]
